title: The three protection arms every bug in this tree gets a verdict for
why: Until this file existed the tree carried sixteen arm names and seventeen result-table shapes, and no reader could answer the one question the corpora are for: for THIS bug, which defence reports and which does not. The mechanism-level arm names stay where they are -- they record how a measurement was produced -- but every one of them now feeds exactly one of the three arms below, and `tools/protection-matrix.py` is the only thing that reads them.

Three arms, because there are three protection levels worth separating: a shipping system that protects the malloc boundary (CheriBSD), Capstone protecting the same boundary, and Capstone protecting the nested allocator's objects as well. The first pair differs by implementation, the second by how deep the protection reaches.

cheribsd.title: stock CheriBSD, revocation at its shipped default
cheribsd.protects: the libc malloc/free boundary: every block is handed out bounded to its usable size, and free quarantines it until a revocation sweep clears the capabilities that pointed into it
cheribsd.revocation: on, asynchronous, quarantine 1/4 of the heap -- the default a CheriBSD system runs with, not a configuration of ours
cheribsd.nested: unprotected: an allocator carving objects out of a malloc block gets no per-object bound and no revocation at its own free
cheribsd.excludes: PoisonCap. It is our adapter for a competitor's platform, so a reader is entitled to discount it; the arm measures what CheriBSD ships. The poisoncap-* arms stay in the cases as a record and are not read here.

capstone-sysalloc.title: Capstone, the libc interface protected
capstone-sysalloc.protects: the same boundary: malloc bounds each object on issue and free revokes it at once, so a capability into a freed object is untagged from the next instruction onwards rather than at the next sweep
capstone-sysalloc.nested: unprotected, exactly as in the cheribsd arm -- which is what makes the two comparable
capstone-sysalloc.vehicle: capstone-virtual, or capstone-baremetal where a corpus has no virtual run

capstone-sublet.title: Capstone, the nested allocator protected too, under the Sublet discipline
capstone-sublet.protects: capstone-sysalloc, plus the program's own allocator issuing each of its objects as a bounded capability and revoking it when the object's life ends -- at whatever granularity the program's own return event has
capstone-sublet.revocation: synchronous, at the nested allocator's own release points
capstone-sublet.nested: protected; this is the only arm in which it is
capstone-sublet.vehicle: capstone-virtual where the port has been lifted onto the application SDK, capstone-baremetal otherwise
capstone-sublet.name: `sublet` here names the discipline the port's adapter follows -- take a linear capability for the block, hand each object out as a bounded sub-capability, give it back when the object's life ends -- which is what `runtime/include/sublet/sublet.h` is and what every in-tree nested adapter is written against.

verdicts.caught: the arm's own mechanism reported: a capability fault with a cause, or SIGPROT with an si_code. Where the case publishes a probe address the fault is required to be at it.
verdicts.missed: the sequence ran to the end and the mechanism said nothing. The case's own DEFECT marker printed, so the defect executed -- a measured silence, not an unexecuted case.
verdicts.wrong-answer: no mechanism fired, and the program's own oracle failed. Counts as not caught; kept distinct because a differential corpus has no fault to wait for.
verdicts.not-run: no measurement exists. Always carries a reason, because 'impossible here', 'waiting on a build' and 'nobody got to it' weigh differently in a denominator.

vehicles.cheribsd-purecap: a CheriBSD process, riscv64-purecap, under CHERI QEMU
vehicles.capstone-virtual: a Linux process under capstone-vexec with capstone_vm.ko, capability pointers over user virtual addresses, full musl libc
vehicles.capstone-baremetal: a freestanding Capstone domain, no libc and no process: the port supplies its memory from a static region. A cell measured here is NOT paired with a capstone-virtual cell -- two things differ, not one -- and the matrix marks it.
